lessons.title: Pointers and (zp),Y
intro: So far, every address was written into the instruction. A pointer is an address stored in memory: two zero page bytes, low byte first.
LDA ($40),Y reads the address stored at $40/$41, adds Y, and loads from there. Change the pointer, and the same instruction reads somewhere else.
Pointers only work in the zero page, and only with Y. Set them up with LDA #<TABLE and LDA #>TABLE, which give the low and high byte of an address.

output: The pointer is $0300, so A = the byte at $0302

exercises.prompt: $40 = $10 and $41 = $03. Where does LDA ($40),Y read when Y = 5?
exercises.explanation: The pointer is $0310, plus Y = 5 gives $0315.

exercises.prompt: Which register works with pointers on the 6502?
exercises.explanation: (zp),Y is the pointer mode. X has a different, rarer one.

exercises.prompt: Store the high byte of TABLE in the pointer.
exercises.explanation: > gives the high byte, < gives the low byte.

exercises.prompt: Why do pointers have to be in the zero page?
options: The instruction only has room for a one-byte address of the pointer
exercises.explanation: LDA ($40),Y is two bytes: the opcode and $40.

exercises.prompt: This should read from $0300, but reads from $0003. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explanation: The low byte goes first. $40 needs $00 and $41 needs $03.

exercises.prompt: Set up a pointer to $0380 at $40/$41.
exercises.explanation: Low byte $80 to $40, high byte $03 to $41.

lessons.title: Copying Blocks
intro: With two pointers, one loop can copy memory from anywhere to anywhere: LDA (from),Y, STA (to),Y, INY, and repeat.
Y goes up to 255, so one round of Y copies up to 256 bytes, a whole page. For more, add 1 to the high bytes of both pointers and start again.
This is how real programs moved text, graphics and data around. Some programs did nothing else all day.

output: Copies 4 bytes from where $40/$41 points to where $42/$43 points

exercises.prompt: How many bytes can one loop with Y copy without changing the pointers?
exercises.explanation: Y goes from 0 to 255: 256 different offsets.

exercises.prompt: What's the advantage of pointers here?
options: The same loop can copy from and to any address
exercises.explanation: Change $40–$43, and the loop copies a different block.

exercises.prompt: Store the byte where the second pointer points.
exercises.explanation: STA (zp),Y writes through a pointer, just like LDA reads.

exercises.prompt: This copy loop never stops. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explanation: DEY counts down from 0 to $FF, $FE … and only reaches 4 much later, after copying the wrong bytes. Use INY.

exercises.prompt: How do you copy the next 256 bytes after the first page?
options: Add 1 to the high bytes of both pointers and start again
exercises.explanation: The pointer's high byte selects the page.

lessons.title: A Print Subroutine
intro: Pointers make subroutines flexible. A PRINT subroutine can print any message: the caller puts the message's address into $40/$41, and PRINT reads it with ($40),Y.
LDA #<MSG and LDA #>MSG give the low and high byte of the label MSG, so the caller never needs to know the actual address.
PRINT loops until it finds the 0 at the end of the message, just like before, only now through the pointer.

exercises.prompt: How does PRINT know which message to print?
options: Its address is in the pointer at $40/$41
exercises.explanation: The caller sets the pointer before JSR PRINT.

options: The low and the high byte of MSG's address
The first and the last letter
exercises.explanation: An address has two bytes, and the pointer needs both.

exercises.prompt: Read the next character through the pointer.
exercises.explanation: ($40),Y reads through the pointer stored at $40/$41.

exercises.prompt: To print a second message MSG2, what do you change?
options: Only the pointer: LDA #<MSG2 and LDA #>MSG2
exercises.explanation: PRINT stays the same. That's the whole point.

exercises.prompt: PRINT prints garbage. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explanation: The low byte goes to $40: LDA #<MSG first. Here the bytes are swapped.
